newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe's office blocks new legal bid over flat.
newsitem.headline: Juppe's office blocks new legal bid over flat.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office blocked an attempt by a Paris taxpayers' association on Thursday to cause him fresh embarrassment over a low-rent city-owned luxury flat he occupied until last year.

The Association for the Defence of Paris Taxpayers sent a bailiff to Juppe's office on Thursday morning with a summons asking him to pay the city of Paris 423,555 francs ($81,058), which it said was the difference between his rent and the market rate, the newspaper Le Monde reported.
But the bailiff did not manage to deliver the summons to the prime minister in person nor to the director of his office.

Juppe, who was assistant mayor for finance when he obtained the apartment in the elegant Saint-Germain-des-Pres district, was forced to move out to avoid a possible conflict of interest prosecution under a ruling by the Paris public prosecutor.

"Having had several previous lawsuits dismissed, notably by the administrative court, this association is relentlessly clutching at any straw," an official in Juppe's office said. "This does not deserve further comment."
However the taxpayers' association said the wording of the administrative court decision to reject its lawsuit left open the possibility of the city seeking reimbursement.

The row over Juppe's apartment, and his procurement of low-rent city-owned flats for his two children, ex-wife and brother-in-law, tarnished his first months in office. It was part of a wider housing scandal which is still smouldering.

Two former ministers in President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR party, Camille Cabana and Robert Pandraud, agreed this year to reimburse the city for the free use of municipal employees as domestic staff at their city-owned flats.
The public prosecutor dropped a case against them in the light of the reimbursements.
